questions.q: Without feature flags, what is true about deploying and releasing a feature?
options: They are always separated by at least one week
They are the same event — the feature becomes live for everyone the moment the deployment finishes
Releasing always happens before deploying
Releasing requires a separate approval from deploying
questions.explain: Without a flag, there's no mechanism to deploy code without it immediately being active for all users — deploy and release collapse into one event.

questions.q: In `client.is_enabled("saved-payment-methods", context={"user_id": request.user.id})`, what is actually being checked?
options: Whether the feature's code exists anywhere in the deployed application
Whether this specific flag is turned on for this specific user, evaluated at request time
Whether the user has a valid payment method on file
Whether the current deployment succeeded
questions.explain: is_enabled asks the flag service, per request and per user context, whether the flag is currently on — independent of whether the code is already deployed.

Shipping code to production with its feature flag turned off, so the deployment itself changes nothing visible to users
A deployment with no logging enabled
A deployment that bypasses all quality gates from Chapter 4
questions.explain: A dark deployment ships the code but keeps the flag off, meaning the deploy itself introduces zero visible change — lowering the risk of the deploy step.

questions.q: Why can a feature flag act as a faster fix than a rollback when a new feature misbehaves?
options: Flipping a flag off is a config change, not a new deployment or build
Flags automatically fix the underlying bug in the code
Rollbacks are always slower than any other operation in Kubernetes
A flag can only be flipped by rebuilding the container image
questions.explain: Turning a flag off is an instant configuration change — no rollback, new build, or pipeline run required, unlike reverting a deployment.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge Retail track an owner and target removal date for every feature flag at creation time?
options: Because flags expire automatically after 24 hours
Because every flag is a permanent code branch that must be maintained, and an unremoved flag after a feature fully ships becomes unnecessary dead code
Because the feature flag SDK requires this metadata to function
Because flags cannot be created without assigning an owner first
questions.explain: A flag left in the code after a feature has fully shipped is a permanent, unnecessary branch — treating removal as a deliberate step prevents that debt from accumulating.
